title: Rescue a no-show before the slot is lost for good
one_liner: When a customer misses an appointment, an AI drafts a kind, no-guilt message offering the next open times, so you can approve it and rebook the visit the same day.
steps: Mark an appointment as a no-show in your booking tool, or let a 15-minute-after-start check flag it.
Pull the next three open slots from your calendar for that service.
An AI step drafts one short message that acknowledges the miss without blame and offers those times.
You approve it in one tap; it sends by text or email, and a reply or booking stops any further messages.
guardrail: A person approves every message, and no fee, penalty or policy is mentioned unless you wrote it into the prompt.
tools: Google Calendar (or your booking tool), Google Sheets or your CRM, n8n or Make, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), Twilio or Gmail
prompt: You write short rebooking messages for [business name], a [type of local business] in [city]. A customer named [first name] missed their [service] appointment on [date and time]. Open times we can offer: [three open slots]. Write one text under 45 words that: acknowledges the missed visit in a warm, no-blame way, offers the open times, and gives [booking link or phone number] to reply. Do not mention fees or penalties unless written here: [cancellation policy or 'none']. Do not guess why they missed it, invent availability, or add urgency. For health-related businesses, never reference the reason for the visit. End with 'Reply STOP to opt out.' Output only the message.
source_name: n8n community templates for no-show recovery (web search results)
verification_note: Given sample slots and a name, the prompt yields a short non-blaming text with the slots and opt-out; fee and urgency are blocked unless supplied.

title: Flag the urgent requests so they get answered first
one_liner: Each new form or email request is read by an AI that tags it urgent, normal or low and writes a two-line summary, so a burst pipe or toothache never waits behind routine questions.
steps: A new request arrives from your website form or contact inbox.
An AI step reads the message and labels it urgent, normal or low using the keywords you define.
Urgent items trigger an immediate text or Slack alert to the on-call person, with a two-line summary.
Everything lands in your CRM or sheet with its label, and a human replies to every request.
guardrail: The AI only sorts and summarizes; a person makes every reply, and for clinics any clinical or emergency judgment stays with staff.
tools: Your website form (Gravity Forms, Typeform), Zapier or Make, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), Google Sheets or your CRM, Slack or Twilio for alerts
prompt: You triage inbound requests for [business name], a [type of local business]. Read the message below and return exactly this: Label: urgent, normal or low. Reason: one short sentence. Summary: two lines with the customer's need, location and preferred timing if stated. Treat as urgent only if it matches: [your urgent keywords, e.g. 'no heat', 'leak', 'flooding', 'severe pain']. If unsure, choose the more urgent label. Do not give advice, diagnoses, prices or promises. Message: [paste request text]. Contact name: [name].
source_name: Zapier and third-party intake guides for home services and dental (web search results)
verification_note: For a sample 'basement flooding' message the prompt returns an urgent label with a short reason and summary and no advice; unclear input defaults to the more urgent label.

title: Build a small playbook of tested prompts your whole team reuses
one_liner: Collect the five or six writing and research tasks your team repeats, test one prompt for each, and keep them in a shared doc so everyone gets the same quality.
steps: List the tasks your team repeats every week, such as quote replies, review replies and customer summaries.
Write one prompt per task with [bracketed] blanks for the details that change.
Test each prompt on three real past examples and edit it until the output needs only light changes.
Save the winners in one shared doc with an owner and a review date, and retire prompts nobody uses.
guardrail: Staff review every output before it reaches a customer, and no customer personal details go into a prompt that isn't approved for it.
tools: Google Docs or Notion, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT)
prompt: Help me turn a repeated task at [business name], a [type of local business] in [city], into a reusable prompt. The task is: [describe the task]. Here are two real examples of past good outputs, with names removed: [example 1] and [example 2]. Write a prompt with [bracketed] placeholders for the details that change each time. State the tone, the length and what to avoid. Then list the three facts a teammate must supply every time. Do not include customer names, prices or promises in the prompt itself.
source_name: Small-business AI threads on Reddit (via web search)
verification_note: Given a task and two examples the prompt produces a reusable template with placeholders and a fact checklist; it avoids embedding names or prices.
